title: Interpretable machine learning for prognostic prediction in critically ill patients with coronary artery disease: a multicenter study
summary: Across 15,930 ICU patients with coronary artery disease in MIMIC-IV, a random-forest model predicted 28-day and 365-day mortality and was evaluated on MIMIC-III. AUCs were 0.858 and 0.851 in internal validation and 0.914 and 0.901 in the external database, respectively. Both cohorts are retrospective database evaluations.
ai_technology: Random-forest mortality models with LASSO feature selection and SHAP interpretation
organization: Wuxi School of Medicine, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, China; Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Wuxi No. 2 People's Hospital (Jiangnan University Medical Center), Wuxi, China; Tianjin Key Laboratory of Ionic-Molecular Function of Cardiovascular Disease, Department of Cardiology, Tianjin Institute of Cardiology, the Second Hospital of Tianjin Medical University, Tianjin, China

evidence.tested: The paper compared seven machine-learning algorithms after feature selection. Random forest performed best for 28-day and 365-day mortality in MIMIC-IV internal validation and MIMIC-III external validation, with AUCs 0.858/0.914 and 0.851/0.901.
evidence.unknown: The validation uses two retrospective MIMIC database cohorts; prospective clinical utility and effects on care or mortality were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO and commonality analysis selected clinical features; random forest estimated 28-day and 365-day mortality risk, and SHAP summarized model feature contributions.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
